title: Decision models on a Mac
evidenceStatus: Full 400-case external test split; 20,000 published distributions independently rescored; two integrity tests passed; frozen main 4c0c40d5; no new inference
summary: The full published comparison is internally reproducible and honestly labeled as synthetic teacher agreement. Fine-tuning improves Laya from 36.35% to 46.95%, but the training prior reaches 48.95%; all five answers match the teacher in only 10/400 tuned cases. Useful deployment needs independent counterfactual outcomes, matched runtime measurements and full export acceptance criteria.
strengths: All 400 external test cases and all 2,000 decisions per model are present; ten model/baseline rows reproduce within 4.3e-9.
Pinned revisions, validation-only selection and a 960/240/400 split with no ID or exact-state overlap.
No silent truncation, actual Core ML full-test predictions and clear warnings about teacher labels, training prior and timing differences.

findings.title: Useful local decision behavior is not established
findings.evidence: probes/local-models.json: tuned 939/2000 versus prior 979/2000; paired case bootstrap difference -2 points, interval -4.8 to +0.8. Whole-case teacher agreement is 10/400 tuned, 30/400 prior, 89/400 Jev.
findings.impact: Training improvement does not establish improvement over a state-independent prior or a reliable multi-field review outcome.
findings.fix: Add independent counterfactual task labels, full-case outcomes and validation-chosen abstention; require utility above prior/code rules.

findings.title: Initial conversion checks determine the export passed flag
findings.evidence: apple/export_coreml.py:198 checks twelve initial outputs. aggregate.py:179 attaches the full test without revising passed. Full export changes 60/2000 argmax choices; maximum probability error 0.14228 and changed-choice MLX margin up to 0.13939.
findings.impact: Conversion success and small parity checks do not establish full decision equivalence, despite accurate UI disclosure of the full result.
findings.fix: Separate conversion, smoke parity and full acceptance flags; test downstream review thresholds and isolate precision/padding/batch effects.

findings.title: Runtime rows execute different workloads
findings.evidence: benchmark_laya.py:26 batches five dynamic rows; benchmark_coreml.py:27 makes five fixed-768 calls. prefill.py:86 excludes tokenization, sequence.py:39 includes branch tokenization. Medians 186.8 versus 555.6 ms reflect these implementations.
findings.impact: The table cannot isolate runtime speed or prefix-cache benefit; there is no matched uncached timing condition.
findings.fix: Measure end-to-end and inference-only time with matched batch/padding conditions, cached/uncached paths, randomized repetitions, cold load and memory.

findings.title: Aggregates obscure constant readouts and probability behavior
findings.evidence: Probe: Qwen 0.6B labels have 10/20 constant-argmax groups; option text has 12/20; tuned Laya and Jev have none. Jev assigns zero to positive teacher mass in 818/2000 decisions; metrics.py uses a shared 1e-12 KL floor.
findings.impact: Readout/label biases and teacher-distribution mismatch remain hard to inspect from workflow averages.
findings.fix: Expose per-question confusion/entropy, label-order and wording tests; calibrate on validation while retaining raw scores.

findings.title: The recorded explorer cannot test a changed fact
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/local-models.tsx:61 and :338 only select model, workflow, case and question; :435 displays immutable state.
findings.impact: Visitors can inspect examples but cannot test a counterexample, correct a field or observe an abstention policy.
findings.fix: Add separate paired-example and editable-review modes with explicit recorded/local/hosted provenance and revision invalidation.

simulation.title: A local-first review desk
simulation.description: Review fictional invoices against orders, change one fact, accept/correct/defer fields and compare branches. Choose local-only or explicit hosted escalation. The current evidence viewer remains recorded.
simulation.jevsRole: Propose typed judgments only on explicit escalation with visible context; never authorize payment.
simulation.codeRole: Own invoice arithmetic, duplicate detection, canonical revisions, edits/undo, review policy, request invalidation and training/test separation.
acceptanceCriteria: No network request in local-only mode and every suggestion names its source/runtime.
Old requests cannot overwrite later edits or restored branches.
Counterfactual facts change required outputs while unrelated accepted fields persist.
Export/MLX differences remain visible at review thresholds.
Complete review outcomes beat the prior at a declared independent task loss; provider failure leaves manual review available.

evaluation.design: Preserve the full official split and existing scoring while adding per-question/whole-case metrics and case-clustered uncertainty. Run five training seeds, frozen test data and a same-data embedding baseline. Add 200 independent counterfactual pairs, 50 per workflow; designate changes/invariances before inference. Three hosted repeats of 400 official plus 400 authored cases require 2400 cases/12000 typed decisions, up to 600 four-case batches before retries. Match timing on 40 stratified cases with ten repetitions and one/five-question cached/uncached workloads.
baselines: Both Qwen readouts and larger untuned model
metrics: Teacher agreement, KL with declared floor, per-option Brier, macro-F1 and ordinal error
Independent rule compliance, counterfactual consistency, review effort and error versus accepted coverage
End-to-end/inference-only p50/p95, cold load, memory and provider failure counts

coverage.current: All 400 official test cases, five questions each, four workflows; 2000 decisions per model. No ID/exact-state overlap with 960 training and 240 validation cases.
coverage.full: Official test split is 400 cases/2000 decisions, already complete at pinned revision ea9306458d6e9563628369a3d1e72e362fb381d2. Proposed 400 counterfactual cases are authored additions, not official rows.
coverage.feasibility: Existing predictions support immediate offline rescoring. Repeated training and matched timing need local compute; new hosted decisions require a request ledger and budget. No new inference occurred.
